newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks pledge not internationally binding - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks pledge not internationally binding - MOF.

text.p: The Japanese Finance Ministry's vow to keep the nation's major banks from failing in cases of severe financial trouble is not a binding international commitment, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Friday.

Mitsuzuka was speaking to a parliamentary committee in response to a question about whether the ministry's so-called "too big to fail" pledge to protect the nation's top 20 banks had the weight of an internationally binding commitment.
"No it is not. It was a vow made from the standpoint of being Japan's finance minister," Mitsuzuka said. He did not elaborate.
